title: Four provinces form Canada
summary: On July 1, Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia form the new Dominion of Canada. Ontario and Quebec are much smaller than they are today. The grey regions have not joined Canada.
watch: Find the four coloured provinces. How different is this from the Canada you know?

title: Manitoba and the Northwest Territories
summary: Rupert’s Land and the North-Western Territory are transferred to Canada. Most of this land becomes the Northwest Territories. Manitoba enters Confederation as a small province around the Red River, following negotiations led by the Métis provisional government.
watch: Look for the original Manitoba. Why is it sometimes called the “postage-stamp province”?

title: British Columbia joins
summary: British Columbia becomes Canada’s sixth province. Its boundary is the one established for the united colony in 1866. Canada now reaches the Pacific coast.
watch: Find British Columbia. Is all the land between it and Ontario part of a province?

title: Prince Edward Island joins
summary: Prince Edward Island becomes the seventh province. The agreement includes Canada taking on the island’s railway debt, buying land from absentee landlords, and providing a connection with the mainland.
watch: Find the small island in the Gulf of St. Lawrence. Use the region list if it is hard to click.

title: Ontario’s provisional boundary grows
summary: The federal government sets provisional northern and western boundaries for Ontario. Ontario’s western boundary remains a source of disagreement with Manitoba.
watch: Compare Ontario with 1873. In which directions has its boundary moved?

title: The District of Keewatin is created
summary: A portion of the Northwest Territories becomes the District of Keewatin. This separate federal district is intended to provide temporary administration for land north and east of Manitoba and west of Ontario.
watch: Find Keewatin. A district is an administrative area; it is not a new province.

title: The Arctic islands become part of Canada
summary: Britain transfers its remaining Arctic territories and islands to Canada. Newfoundland remains outside Confederation. The transferred islands become part of the Northwest Territories.
watch: Look north. Which large grey region has changed to a Canadian territory?

title: Manitoba expands
summary: Manitoba’s boundaries move west, north, and east. Ontario objects to the eastern extension, so the map marks a disputed area between the two provinces.
watch: Find the striped disputed area. How can a map show that a boundary is not agreed upon?

title: Four western districts are established
summary: Assiniboia, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and Athabasca become provisional districts within the Northwest Territories. These districts help administer the region as settlement and railway construction increase.
watch: Find the Alberta district. Does it have the same outline as the province today?

title: Keewatin’s boundary is adjusted
summary: The southwestern boundary of the District of Keewatin is adjusted to fit the boundaries of the western districts created in 1882.
watch: Turn on previous boundaries and look at Keewatin’s southwestern edge.

title: Ontario and Manitoba’s dispute is settled
summary: The Ontario Boundary Act settles the Ontario–Manitoba boundary dispute. Ontario extends west to Lake of the Woods and north to the Albany River.
watch: Compare 1881 and 1889. What has happened to the striped area?

title: The northern districts are reorganized
summary: Ungava, Mackenzie, Yukon, and Franklin are established as additional districts in the Northwest Territories. Athabasca and Keewatin are enlarged.
watch: Locate Yukon and Ungava. What are these areas called on a later map?

title: Northern district boundaries change
summary: The boundaries of Franklin, Keewatin, Mackenzie, Ungava, and Yukon districts are adjusted. These are changes to administrative districts rather than the creation of provinces.
watch: Use previous boundaries to compare the northern districts with 1895.

title: Yukon becomes a separate territory
summary: Yukon is separated from the Northwest Territories to become Yukon Territory. Quebec’s northern boundary extends to the Eastmain River.
watch: Find Yukon Territory, then compare Quebec with the previous map.

title: Yukon’s boundary is adjusted
summary: Yukon Territory’s boundaries are adjusted to the outline shown in later Atlas snapshots.
watch: Look closely at Yukon with previous boundaries switched on. Some changes are much smaller than others.

title: Alberta and Saskatchewan become provinces
summary: Alberta and Saskatchewan are created from the Northwest Territories. Canada now has nine provinces. Keewatin is returned to the Northwest Territories and continues as one of its districts.
watch: Compare the new provinces with the earlier western districts. Which boundaries have disappeared?

title: Three provinces extend north
summary: Manitoba, Ontario, and Quebec extend northward. Ungava becomes part of Quebec, and Keewatin loses much of its land. Offshore islands are not included in Quebec’s extension.
watch: Compare these three provinces with 1905. Which reaches Hudson Strait?

title: Northern district boundaries are defined
summary: The boundaries of districts within the Northwest Territories are formally redescribed. This records changes following the creation of Alberta and Saskatchewan and the northern extensions of Manitoba, Ontario, and Quebec.
watch: Look at Mackenzie, Keewatin, and Franklin. These are districts within the Northwest Territories.

title: The Labrador boundary is defined
summary: The British Privy Council defines the boundary between Canada and Newfoundland in Labrador. Newfoundland is still outside Confederation at this point. The Atlas shows the boundary established by this decision.
watch: Compare Labrador with 1920. Why is Newfoundland still grey?

title: Newfoundland joins Canada
summary: On March 31, Newfoundland enters Confederation as Canada’s tenth province. It includes the island of Newfoundland and Labrador on the mainland.
watch: Find both parts of the new province. What has changed since 1927?

title: Nunavut is created
summary: On April 1, the eastern part of the Northwest Territories becomes Nunavut. Its creation follows years of Inuit work and negotiations, including the 1993 Nunavut Land Claims Agreement. Canada now has three territories.
watch: Compare Nunavut with the remaining Northwest Territories. Why might new boundaries matter to the people living there?

title: Newfoundland and Labrador
summary: On December 6, the province’s official name changes from Newfoundland to Newfoundland and Labrador. This is a name change, not a boundary change.
watch: Look at the province’s outline and its label. Which has changed?

title: Yukon’s official name changes
summary: The new Yukon Act takes effect on April 1. The official name changes from Yukon Territory to Yukon. The territorial boundary remains the same.
watch: Compare Yukon with 2001. Can a map change even when its boundary stays the same?
